item.title: For some Christians, Hegseth's plan for public execution fits a biblical mandate
item.description: Defense Secretary Hegseth's announcement of a livestreamed execution elicited reactions of disgust and condemnation from some faith leaders and politicians. But within his church, it's not an outlier.

item.title: LA fire survivors face another setback with FEMA program delays
item.description: The fight over a FEMA program aiding some of LA's most vulnerable wildfire victims is the latest setback for hundreds of fire survivors who still haven't rebuilt after the deadly 2025 infernos.
item.content:encoded: The fight over a FEMA program aiding some of LA's most vulnerable wildfire victims is the latest setback for hundreds of fire survivors who still haven't rebuilt after the deadly 2025 infernos.

item.title: Social Security could soon run out of money. Here are some possible solutions
item.description: Social Security may run short of money to make full payments to retirees as soon as 2032. The team from NPR's Planet Money examines possible solutions.
item.content:encoded: Social Security may run short of money to make full payments to retirees as soon as 2032. The team from NPR's Planet Money examines possible solutions.

item.title: Wyoming tribes ask church pastor to leave after viral sermon
item.description: Tribes on the Wind River Reservation in Wyoming are asking a Christian pastor to leave after she denigrated their native religion in a sermon.
item.content:encoded: Tribes on the Wind River Reservation in Wyoming are asking a Christian pastor to leave after she denigrated their native religion in a sermon.

item.title: USS Abraham Lincoln returns home as Navy navigates lengthy deployments among crews
item.description: The crew of USS Abraham Lincoln is now home, tired and ready for the next chapter. But the Navy is grappling with crews still at sea with lengthy deployments as the U.S. war with Iran continues.

item.title: A rocky first press briefing for a rookie White House press secretary
item.description: Katie Zacharia's first White House press briefing was short and often halting. The new press secretary chosen by President Trump left a lot of unanswered questions, including some uncertainties about her own qualifications.

item.title: Cornell's president has not resigned despite heavy scrutiny
item.description: The president of Cornell University, Michael Kotlikoff, is under fire over the university's handling of a gang rape at a fraternity party in 2024.

item.title: In Kansas, a newly competitive Senate race tests limit of Trump's unpopular policies
item.description: Kansas voters could send a Democrat to the Senate for the first time in nearly a century — and flip the governor's office back to Republican control, even in what could be a tough year for the GOP.

item.title: 'They're stealing from the poor': A major source of SNAP fraud robs recipients of millions
item.description: Organized criminal rings target SNAP recipients because of the government program's outdated security features. But upgrading the tech costs money and states' SNAP budgets are getting squeezed.

item.title: Labor Department to release latest inflation report
item.description: Higher energy prices, tied to the U.S. war with Iran, are driving up the overall cost-of-living. The Labor Department is set to deliver its latest inflation report this morning.
